proofs.proof_tex:
Under \(ass:one-unsupported-row\) and \(ass:binary-free-row\), the generalized objects specialize as
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},\qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}=\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq1\}.
\]
The class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is then exactly \(Mone\), \(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is \(Q\), and the replay defining \(\Phi\) is the replay defining \(F\).  This last equality is also the content of \(lem:polynomial-reduction\).  The generalized sharpness theorem therefore yields
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1]),
\]
and its endpoint-model construction realizes every \(q\in[0,1]\) by a common finite-noise, type-shared RSCM reproducing \(Psrc\).  Thus this equality is compatibility sharp, not merely an outer bound.

We next identify the algebraic endpoints.  A polynomial is continuous, and the compact-attainment argument in \(thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows\) supplies minimizers and maximizers on \([0,1]\).  If a nonconstant \(F\) has an optimizer \(c\in(0,1)\), then for sufficiently small positive and negative \(h\), the difference quotients
\[
 \frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}
\]
have opposite weak signs.  Their common limit is \(F'(c)\), so \(F'(c)=0\).  Hence every optimizer is either a boundary point or a feasible derivative root and belongs to \(Ccrit\).  If \(F\) is constant, every candidate has the same value.  In both cases, the definitions of \(L\) and \(U\) give
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=U.
\]
The continuous scalar-image argument in the generalized theorem then gives \(F([0,1])=[L,U]\), proving the first claim.

The cited scope result records that the comparator's \(\rho\)-Markovian class allows shared exogenous parents within an instance.  A model in \(Mone\) has the special case of no such shared exogenous parent because \(ass:markovian-noises\) makes all ground-variable noises mutually independent.  Its observed domains are finite by \(ass:finite-domains\), and on the fixed finite graph its relational-parent multiset size has a finite uniform maximum.  Consequently \(Mone\) is a subclass of the comparator class, and it can be a strict subclass when the graph permits the additional confounding.

If \(F\) is nonconstant, choose \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) with \(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  Sharpness provides models \(M_{q_1},M_{q_2}\in Mone\) with these two causal values.  They also lie in the larger class, so that class cannot point identify the query.  A \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) report is therefore accompanied here by an exact range only for the fully Markovian subclass; no step has bounded the extra confounded models.  If \(F\) is constant, all models in \(Mone\) have the single value \(L=U\).  The same conclusion holds for the comparator class when the supplied graph rules out its extra shared-exogenous structures and the classes consequently coincide.  Without that equality, constancy on a subclass cannot determine values on its strict superclass.

Finally, unsupportedness alone cannot force failure because the target functional may cancel the free row.  The role of type sharing is load bearing: with two independent target nodes using the same unsupported binary key and event \(B\) equal to ``exactly one success,'' the shared-row polynomial is \(2q(1-q)\leq1/2\); if type sharing is removed, choosing the two occurrence probabilities as one and zero makes the event probability one, outside the asserted one-parameter range.  Conversely, a supported outcome row that is the same for both values of an unsupported upstream node makes \(F\) constant, so a complete procedure may identify the query despite the unsupported key.  These finite examples verify both the specialization and its stated qualification.

If \(Cn=\varnothing\), the pointwise assertion is vacuous and the definition returns \(Kn=[0,1]\).  Now fix an outcome for which \(Cn\neq\varnothing\), so the deterministic feasible center \(etahat\in Cn\) exists.  For every \(eta\in Cn\), supported row \(r\), and category \(y\), both \(eta_{r,y}\) and \(\widehat\eta_{r,y}\) lie in \([\ell_{r,y},u_{r,y}]\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\eta_r,\widehat\eta_r)
 =\frac12\sum_y|\eta_{r,y}-\widehat\eta_{r,y}|
 \leq\frac12\sum_y
 \max\!\left\{|\ell_{r,y}-\widehat\eta_{r,y}|,
                  |u_{r,y}-\widehat\eta_{r,y}|\right\}
 \leq\epsilon_r.
\]
The last inequality also uses that total variation between two categorical laws is at most one, exactly as in the definition of \(\epsilon_r\).

Fix \(q\in[0,1]\) and couple the target systems with supported rows \(eta\) and \(etahat\) in a topological order of the intervened acyclic ground graph.  Intervened nodes are set equal.  Conditional on no earlier disagreement, the two systems have the same realized parents at the current node and therefore the same type--context label, although that label may depend on the common realized history.  At the unsupported key \(rstar\), use the same draw from \((1-q,q)\), which has disagreement probability zero.

At a supported row \(r\), put \(c_y=\min\{\eta_{r,y},\widehat\eta_{r,y}\}\) and \(s=\sum_yc_y\).  Assign mass \(c_y\) to the matched pair \((y,y)\).  If \(s<1\), assign residual mass
\[
 \frac{(\eta_{r,y}-c_y)(\widehat\eta_{r,z}-c_z)}{1-s}
\]
to \((y,z)\); if \(s=1\), there is no residual part.  Direct summation gives marginals \(\eta_r\) and \(\widehat\eta_r\).  For each \(y\), at least one of \(\eta_{r,y}-c_y\) and \(\widehat\eta_{r,y}-c_y\) is zero, so the residual law has no diagonal mass.  Its disagreement probability is therefore
\[
 1-s=\operatorname{TV}(\eta_r,\widehat\eta_r)\leq\epsilon_r.
\]
Fresh coupling randomness at each ground node preserves the required conditional marginal in each system, as required by \(ass:markovian-noises\).

By definition, \(m_r\) is a pathwise upper bound on the number of target occurrences carrying label \(r\).  The hypotheses of \(lem:multiplicative-occurrence-radius\) therefore hold even though the labels are history dependent.  It follows that
\[
 \Pr(\text{some target-node disagreement})
 \leq\delta
 =1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}
 \leq\min\left\{1,\sum_rm_r\epsilon_r\right\}.
\]
The indicators of \(B\) in the two systems can differ only if some target node differs.  Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |H(eta,q)-H(etahat,q)|
 &=\left|\mathbb E\{\mathbf 1_B(X)-\mathbf 1_B(\widehat X)\}\right|\\
 &\leq\mathbb E|\mathbf 1_B(X)-\mathbf 1_B(\widehat X)|\\
 &\leq\Pr(X\neq\widehat X)\leq\delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the uniform pointwise assertion.

Let \(E_n=\{eta0\in Cn\}\).  The sampling-context positivity assumption makes every population conditional row in \(eta0\) well defined, and joint box coverage gives \(\Pr(E_n)\geq1-\alpha\).  On \(E_n\), the polytope is nonempty and the uniform inequality applies with \(eta=eta0\).  Since \(Lhat\) and \(Uhat\) are respectively the minimum and maximum of the center polynomial over \([0,1]\), for every \(q\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Lhat-\delta\leq H(eta0,q)\leq Uhat+\delta.
\]
The functional \(H\) is a probability, so intersecting this interval with \([0,1]\) preserves inclusion.  By the corrected definition of \(Kn\),
\[
 \{H(eta0,q):q\in[0,1]\}\subseteq Kn
\]
on \(E_n\).  Its probability is at least \(1-\alpha\).  The construction optimizes only the center polynomial in the unsupported coordinate and inflates it uniformly; it does not optimize jointly over \(eta\in Cn\), so no exact multivariate-projection claim is made.

added_lemmas.statement:
The set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) is finite, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\) is a nonempty finite product of finite-dimensional probability simplices, and \(\Phi\) is a multivariate polynomial with rational coefficients in the coordinates \(p_{r,y}\).  For every \(M\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\), its type-shared unsupported conditional rows form a vector \(p_M\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\) and
\[
 Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M)=\Phi(p_M).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(ass:finite-domains\), every outcome alphabet is finite.  The target grounding \(\rho\) and its explicit incidence table \(Ictx\) are finite, so only finitely many type--context keys occur in event-consistent target terms.  Hence the subset \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) is finite.  Every simplex \(\Delta_r\) contains, for example, each point mass on \(\mathcal Y_r\), so their finite product \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\) is nonempty; if \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\varnothing\), this is the stipulated singleton product.

Fix an event-consistent complete assignment \(x\) of the nonintervened target nodes.  Acyclicity from \(ass:acyclic-groundings\) gives a topological ordering, and independent ground noises from \(ass:markovian-noises\) give the truncated Markov factorization
\[
 P_M^\rho(x\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =\prod_{v\notin\operatorname{dom}(a)}
 P_M\!\left(x_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}(v)}\right).
\]
By \(ass:type-sharing\), the factor at \(v\) depends on its type--context key rather than on the occurrence label.  If that key has a source occurrence with parent context \(c\) of positive probability, its row is recovered coordinatewise as
\[
 K_r(y)=\frac{Psrc(Y=y,C=c)}{Psrc(C=c)}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive by the definition of positive source support, both numerator and denominator are rational because the tables \(Psrc\) are rational, and \(ass:source-compatibility\) makes this ratio independent of the chosen positive-support occurrence.  Thus the supported factor is uniquely recovered and rational.  Otherwise the key belongs to \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) by \(def:finite-unsupported-parameter-space\), and the factor is one coordinate \(p_{r,x_v}\).  Hence each assignment probability is a monomial in the coordinates of \(p\), multiplied by a rational coefficient.  There are finitely many assignments, and summing the monomials for \(B\) is exactly the replay in \(def:multivariate-target-polynomial\).  Therefore \(\Phi\in\mathbb Q[(p_{r,y})]\).

Now take \(M\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\).  Each unrestricted finite categorical conditional row is a probability vector, and type sharing assigns one such vector to every key, so their collection \(p_M\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\).  Applying the preceding factorization with these actual rows makes its assignment-by-assignment sum equal both to \(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M)\) and to \(\Phi(p_M)\).  This proves the displayed equality.
added_lemmas.justification: This exposes the structural finite-dimensional parameterization before any optimization algorithm is chosen.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing one-row algebra does not establish the causal reduction for a product of shared categorical mechanism rows.
added_lemmas.consumer: Relational queries with several source-unsupported contexts obtain an explicit sharp optimization domain.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(p_0\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\), there is a finite-noise model \(M_{p_0}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) that reproduces every source law in \(Psrc\), uses independent copies of one common noise law and one common mechanism for each endogenous type, has unsupported rows \(p_0\), and satisfies \(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M_{p_0})=\Phi(p_0)\).  If \(\mathcal C_t(p_0)\) is the set of distinct positive-probability source rows and free target rows of a type \(t\) with alphabet size \(k_t\), the construction uses at most
\[
 1+|\mathcal C_t(p_0)|(k_t-1)
\]
positive noise atoms for that type.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(p_0\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\).  For every endogenous type \(t\), order its finite alphabet as \(\{1,\ldots,k_t\}\).  Let \(\mathcal C_t(p_0)\) contain every distinct conditional row of type \(t\) recovered from a positive-probability source parent context and every row of \(p_0\) having type \(t\).  Source compatibility ensures that a row recovered at two source occurrences is the same row, so this collection is well defined.  For \(c\in\mathcal C_t(p_0)\), write
\[
 b_{c,j}=\sum_{h=1}^j p_{c,h},\qquad j=0,\ldots,k_t,
\]
with \(b_{c,0}=0\) and \(b_{c,k_t}=1\).  Sort the distinct numbers in
\[
 \{0,1\}\cup\{b_{c,j}:c\in\mathcal C_t(p_0),\ 1\leq j<k_t\}
\]
as \(0=d_{t,0}<d_{t,1}<\cdots<d_{t,h_t}=1\).  Give the type-\(t\) noise the finite atoms \(j=1,\ldots,h_t\) with masses \(d_{t,j}-d_{t,j-1}>0\).

For each atom choose any \(u_{t,j}\in(d_{t,j-1},d_{t,j})\).  Define the common type mechanism at context \(c\) to output the unique category \(y\) such that
\[
 b_{c,y-1}<u_{t,j}<b_{c,y},
\]
with empty zero-probability categories skipped.  No cumulative threshold lies in the open atom interval, so the selected category is independent of the chosen interior point.  The intervals whose output is at most \(y\) have total mass \(b_{c,y}\); subtraction at consecutive thresholds therefore shows that the probability of output \(y\) is
\[
 b_{c,y}-b_{c,y-1}=p_{c,y}.
\]
For a context absent from \(\mathcal C_t(p_0)\), choose an arbitrary fixed category.  This choice can affect neither a positive-probability source cell nor a target term using a supported or free target-relevant key.

Give distinct ground nodes mutually independent copies of the noise belonging to their type and use the single context-indexed mechanism just defined for that type.  Thus ground noises are independent and mechanisms are type shared.  On a source grounding, topological induction using \(ass:acyclic-groundings\) shows that every positive-probability parent context has exactly its recovered conditional row.  The source joint law is consequently the product of these rows.  By \(ass:source-compatibility\), this product is the given rational table in \(Psrc\); rows at zero-probability parent contexts do not change it.  Hence the constructed model belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\), and its free rows are exactly \(p_0\).

The multivariate polynomial reduction now gives
\[
 Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M_{p_0})=\Phi(p_0).
\]
There are at most \(|\mathcal C_t(p_0)|(k_t-1)\) distinct interior cumulative thresholds.  Together with \(0\) and \(1\), they create at most \(1+|\mathcal C_t(p_0)|(k_t-1)\) positive adjacent-interval atoms, proving the stated atom bound.  Coincident thresholds only reduce this number.
added_lemmas.justification: Sharpness over several rows requires compatible common RSCMs realizing every simplex parameter vector.
added_lemmas.gap: A multivariate polynomial image is not causally sharp until every parameter vector is realized under type sharing and independent ground noises.
added_lemmas.consumer: Endpoint solutions of any exact or approximate multivariate optimizer can be serialized as finite relational SCM witnesses.

added_lemmas.statement:
The compatible causal set for any finite family of unsupported finite-categorical rows is
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}=\Phi(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}})
 =\left[\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}}\Phi(p),
         \max_{p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}}\Phi(p)\right].
\]
Both endpoints are attained by finite-noise, type-shared models in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\).  This is a structural sharpness statement; it does not assert an efficient exact algorithm for optimizing a general multivariate \(\Phi\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The multivariate reduction gives
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}\subseteq\Phi(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}).
\]
Conversely, for every \(p_0\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\), the finite-noise construction supplies \(M_{p_0}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) with \(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M_{p_0})=\Phi(p_0)\).  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}=\Phi(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}).
\]

It remains to characterize this scalar image.  Write all free row coordinates in a fixed finite vector in \([0,1]^d\).  Given any sequence in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\), repeated interval bisection produces a subsequence converging in its first coordinate; iterating over the finitely many coordinates and taking the final diagonal subsequence gives a coordinatewise convergent subsequence.  Every coordinate limit is nonnegative, and taking limits in each finite row sum preserves \(\sum_y p_{r,y}=1\).  Hence the limit remains in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\).  When \(d=0\), the product is already a singleton.  Thus every sequence in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\) has a convergent subsequence whose limit stays in the set.

Let \(u\) be the supremum of \(\Phi(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}})\) and choose \(p_j\) with \(\Phi(p_j)\to u\).  A convergent subsequence has limit \(p^+\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\).  Since a polynomial is continuous, \(\Phi(p^+)=u\).  The same argument for the infimum gives \(p^-\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\) attaining the minimum \(l\).

The product of simplices is convex: for \(t\in[0,1]\), every row of \((1-t)p^-+tp^+\) remains nonnegative and sums to one.  Therefore
\[
 g(t)=\Phi((1-t)p^-+tp^+)
\]
is a continuous univariate polynomial with \(g(0)=l\) and \(g(1)=u\).  For any \(z\in[l,u]\), bisect \([0,1]\) repeatedly, each time retaining a half whose endpoint values bracket \(z\).  The nested intervals have a common limit point \(t_z\), and continuity gives \(g(t_z)=z\).  Hence the image contains all of \([l,u]\), while the definitions of \(l\) and \(u\) give the reverse inclusion.  Finally, applying the finite-noise construction to \(p^-\) and \(p^+\) gives endpoint-attaining models in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This is the maximal structural identified-set theorem for finitely many unsupported finite-categorical shared rows.
added_lemmas.gap: The causal literature does not turn this relational support pattern into an exact product-simplex image with attaining common finite-noise models.
added_lemmas.consumer: Future multivariate solvers may optimize the explicit polynomial without reopening the causal soundness and sharpness argument.

added_lemmas.statement:
Consider any finite sequential coupling in which, conditional on no earlier disagreement, the current supported row label \(r\) may depend on the common observed history, its conditional disagreement probability is at most \(\epsilon_r\), and every no-disagreement history uses label \(r\) at most \(m_r\) times.  With a zero-exponent factor defined as one,
\[
 \Pr(\text{some disagreement})\leq
 \delta=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}
 \leq\min\left\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\right\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(b_r=1-\epsilon_r\in[0,1]\), with \(b_r^0=1\) also when \(b_r=0\).  View the finite sequential construction as a decision tree whose nodes are common histories reached without a disagreement.  At a history where the current label is \(r\), the total conditional probability of matched children is at least \(b_r\).  Along every root-to-leaf common history, label \(r\) occurs at most \(m_r\) times.

We prove a survival lower bound by backward induction.  At a history that has already used label \(r\) exactly \(k_r\) times, the conditional probability of reaching a leaf without disagreement is at least
\[
 \prod_r b_r^{m_r-k_r}.
\]
At a leaf this holds because the left side is one and every factor on the right lies in \([0,1]\).  At an internal history with current label \(s\), each matched child has count vector \(k+e_s\), so the induction hypothesis bounds its future survival by
\[
 \prod_r b_r^{m_r-k_r-\mathbf 1\{r=s\}}.
\]
Summing over matched children and using that their total conditional mass is at least \(b_s\) gives the claimed bound at the parent.  At the root, therefore,
\[
 \Pr(\text{no disagreement})\geq\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r},
\]
which proves the first inequality after taking complements.  This induction permits the label at each step to be an arbitrary function of the common history.

For the comparison with the additive radius, list \(m_r\) copies of each number \(\epsilon_r\) as \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\).  The identity
\[
 1-\prod_{j=1}^N(1-x_j)
 =1-\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-x_j)+x_N\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-x_j)
\]
and induction give \(1-\prod_j(1-x_j)\leq\sum_jx_j=\sum_rm_r\epsilon_r\).  The same left side lies in \([0,1]\), proving the clipped bound.
added_lemmas.justification: The product survival probability strictly improves the additive union radius while allowing history-dependent relational row labels.
added_lemmas.gap: A plain telescoping union bound does not exploit sequential survival across repeated labeled occurrences.
added_lemmas.consumer: Finite-sample traffic enclosures receive a uniformly no-wider occurrence-coupling inflation.

added_lemmas.statement: The Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian RSCM class has finite observed domains and uniformly bounded relational-parent multisets, permits within-instance latent confounding through shared exogenous parents, and is the domain of their complete relational identification procedure and neural identified-case criterion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Within the fully Markovian class \(Mone\), the compatible causal set is exactly
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]
The Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian class may be strictly larger because it permits within-instance latent confounding.  If \(F\) is nonconstant, nonidentification transfers to that larger class by subclass inclusion.  If their complete procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), \([L,U]\) remains the sharp set for \(Mone\) but is not asserted to be sharp for the larger class.  If \(F\) is constant, then \(L=U\) identifies the query over \(Mone\); this point-identification conclusion transfers to the Ejaz--Bareinboim class only when the supplied graph excludes the additional confounding so that the two classes coincide.  The unsupported status of \(rstar\) alone does not imply \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old comparator sentence transferred a singleton conclusion from the fully Markovian subclass to a larger rho-Markovian class that can include latent-confounded models. The corrected claim retains exact sharpness for the stated class, transfers nonidentification upward by subclass inclusion, and transfers point identification only under class equality.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Choose rational \(etahat\in Cn\) when \(Cn\neq\varnothing\), compute \(epsilon\), set
\[
 \delta=\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r},
\]
where a zero-exponent factor is one, compute \([Lhat,Uhat]=H(etahat,[0,1])\), and return \(Kn=[\max\{0,Lhat-\delta\},\min\{1,Uhat+\delta\}]\); return \([0,1]\) when \(Cn=\varnothing\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Sequential maximal coupling yields the smaller multiplicative disagreement radius, while the previous construction stored only its additive union-bound relaxation.

proposed.name: Finite unsupported-row product simplex
proposed.construction:
Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) be the set of type--context keys that occur in an event-consistent target term recorded by \(Ictx\) but whose parent-context event has probability zero at every source occurrence.  If \(\mathcal Y_r\) is the finite outcome alphabet of \(r\), put
\[
 \Delta_r=\left\{(p_{r,y})_{y\in\mathcal Y_r}:p_{r,y}\geq0,\ \sum_{y\in\mathcal Y_r}p_{r,y}=1\right\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}=\prod_{r\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}}\Delta_r,
\]
where the empty product is a singleton.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the explicit optimization domain for any finite unsupported categorical family.

proposed.name: Multivariate relational target polynomial
proposed.construction: For \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}\), \(\Phi(p)\) is obtained by replaying the finite truncated target factorization encoded by \(S,G,\rho,a,B,Ictx\), substituting the rational supported rows \(K\) and substituting \(p_{r,y}\) whenever an occurrence has key \(r\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The causal factorization must be named separately from its sharp image.

proposed.name: Finite-unsupported-row compatible RSCM class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is the class of finite RSCMs over \(S\) and \(G\) that induce the source groundings \(Rsrc\) and target grounding \(\rho\) encoded by \(Ictx\), have mutually independent ground-variable noises and type-shared finite mechanisms, reproduce \(Psrc\), use the recovered rows \(K\) at every target-relevant positive-source-support key, and leave precisely the target-relevant keys in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) unrestricted over their native finite outcome alphabets.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This class generalizes the structural result without changing the one-row certificate class.

proposed.name: Finite-unsupported-row causal identified set
proposed.construction: For \(M\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\), let \(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M)=P_M^{\rho}(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))\), and define \(\Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}=\{Q_{\mathrm{fin}}(M):M\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\}\).

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite family of target-relevant unsupported finite-categorical shared rows, the fully Markovian relational causal set is exactly the compact interval obtained as the image of an explicit rational polynomial over the product of the row simplices, and both endpoints have common finite-noise type-shared RSCM witnesses. The one unsupported binary row remains the tractable specialization: derivative-root isolation gives exact algebraic endpoints and the skeptical certificate checks the complete explicit relational instance and endpoint models with polynomial size and checking cost. This sharp interval is for the independent-ground-noise class; the Ejaz--Bareinboim rho-Markovian class is larger when within-instance latent confounding is allowed, so only nonidentification transfers upward automatically. Supported-row boxes use the sharper multiplicative radius \(\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}\), which is no larger than the additive union radius. A treewidth-zero witness with nontrivial query \(B=\{X_1=X_{k+1}\}\), \(F=1/2\), and direct unsupported-row relevance forces \(2^k\) records only because the frozen checker demands exhaustive assignment-level \(Ictx\); compact circuit-level incidence remains open.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the multivariate structural sharp image with finite-noise endpoint witnesses, retains a sound and complete polynomial-size skeptical certificate for the univariate specialization, and supplies a conservative sampling enclosure using a history-adaptive multiplicative occurrence-coupling radius.

prose_updates.related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim define the larger rho-Markovian RSCM class, which permits within-instance latent confounding under finite observed domains and uniformly bounded relational-parent multisets, and give complete identification and neural identified-case results there. The present exact image is proved for the fully Markovian subclass with mutually independent ground-variable noises and no shared exogenous parent. A nonconstant image supplies two subclass witnesses and therefore proves nonidentification in the larger class, but neither the subclass interval nor a constant subclass polynomial transfers as a sharp range or point-identification result unless the supplied graph excludes the additional confounding and the classes coincide. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide canonical finite-SCM polynomial programs, and Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxations; neither supplies this relational product-simplex realization theorem, exact univariate relational certificate, or multiplicative labeled-occurrence enclosure. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply the skeptical algebraic and root-isolation substrate. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein identify a polynomial explicit-univariate model-checking core. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining models for order-based nonrelational bounds, but their witnesses do not impose the present type-shared independent-ground-noise semantics.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Efficient exact optimization and skeptical certification of a general multivariate product-simplex polynomial remain open; the complete exact certificate here is univariate. The frozen certificate transaction also requires exhaustive event-consistent assignment records in \(Ictx\). Even for an edgeless target with \(w=0\), the nontrivial query \(B=\{X_1=X_{k+1}\}\), a fair supported \(X_1\), and unsupported-row \(X_{k+1}\) has \(F=1/2\) and direct relevance but forces \(2^k\) records. This is an obstruction to width-sensitive production for the frozen exhaustive grammar only; a circuit-level incidence grammar and checker remain open. The confidence interval is conservative and is not the exact projection over supported-row boxes.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Structural soundness, completeness, compact interval form, endpoint attainment, and the finite breakpoint atom-count bound are proved for any finite family of unsupported finite-categorical rows in fully observed, acyclic, fully Markovian type-shared RSCMs. Exact derivative-root optimization, algebraic endpoint comparison, polynomial-size certificates, the sharp optimizer-degree guarantee, and the at-most-two algebraic-noise-mass guarantee remain specific to the one unsupported binary row. The interval is not claimed sharp for the larger rho-Markovian class when latent confounding is allowed. Efficient exact multivariate optimization, compact circuit-level incidence, conditional postintervention queries, exact nuisance-box projection, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. The sampling enclosure has simultaneous coverage and uses \(\delta_{\times}\leq\min\{1,\sum_rm_r\epsilon_r\}\); it is deliberately conservative. As sanity reductions, \(F(q)=q\) gives \([0,1]\), while a constant \(F\) gives a singleton only for the stated fully Markovian class unless the comparator classes coincide.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(k\geq 1\).  We construct the promised instance explicitly.  Take a fixed relational schema with two binary endogenous attribute types, denoted \(A\) and \(C\), and a relational causal graph with no directed edges.  A source grounding contains one isolated node of type \(A\), and its source table assigns probabilities \(1/2\) and \(1/2\) to the two outcomes.  Thus this row has positive rational source support and is contained in \(K\).  The target grounding contains isolated binary nodes \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\) of type \(A\) in that supported context and one isolated binary node \(X_{k+1}\) of type \(C\) in a context absent from every source grounding.  Declare that last type--context key to be \(rstar\).  There are no other target type--context keys, so \(rstar\) is the unique unsupported target key.  Use the empty intervention and the event
\[
 B_k=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}:x_1=x_{k+1}\}.
\]
All domains are finite as required by \texttt{ass:finite-domains}.  The ground graph has no edges, so it is acyclic as required by \texttt{ass:acyclic-groundings}.  Moreover, the singleton bags \(\{X_j\}\), joined in any tree, form a tree decomposition of width \(1-1=0\).  Hence \(w=0\).  The schema and source grounding have constant size, the target node list has \(k+1\) entries and no edge list, and the event is encoded by two node indices using \(O(\log(k+1))\) bits.  Thus the complete pre-incidence input encoding has size \(O(k)\) under the canonical ordered-node representation.

Assign the same fair row to every occurrence \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\).  This satisfies \texttt{ass:type-sharing}.  At \(X_{k+1}\), assign the shared binary row
\[
 \pi_q(z)=(1-q)^{1-z}q^z,\qquad z\in\{0,1\},\quad q\in[0,1].
\]
For completeness, these rows have a finite Markovian realization: give every ground node an independent two-atom noise, use masses \((1/2,1/2)\) for type \(A\), masses \((1-q,q)\) for type \(C\) in context \(rstar\), and let the structural mechanism output the atom label.  Consequently the constructed source law is reproduced exactly for every \(q\in[0,1]\), including the boundary cases \(q=0\) and \(q=1\).  The node \(X_{k+1}\) is not intervened upon and occurs explicitly in the defining equality for \(B_k\).  Every assignment term consistent with \(B_k\) therefore contains the factor \(\pi_q(x_{k+1})\) labeled by \(rstar\).  By the target-relevance and incidence clauses in the definition of \(Ictx\), this makes \(rstar\) directly event-relevant, even though the sum below cancels its parameter.

By the definition of \(F\), replaying the truncated factorization gives, for every \(q\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F_k(q)
 &=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}:\,x_1=x_{k+1}}
      \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac12\right)
      (1-q)^{1-x_{k+1}}q^{x_{k+1}}. 
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(x_{k+1}=0\), the equality forces \(x_1=0\), while \(x_2,\ldots,x_k\) are free.  Hence that part of the sum contains \(2^{k-1}\) terms and equals
\[
 2^{k-1}2^{-k}(1-q)=\frac{1-q}{2}.
\]
For \(x_{k+1}=1\), the equality forces \(x_1=1\), again leaving \(2^{k-1}\) choices, so the second part equals
\[
 2^{k-1}2^{-k}q=\frac q2.
\]
Adding the two displayed quantities yields
\[
 F_k(q)=\frac{1-q}{2}+\frac q2=\frac12.
\]
Thus the dense output polynomial is the constant \(F=1/2\).  The event is not the sure event: for example, the assignment with \(x_1=0\) and \(x_{k+1}=1\) is excluded.  The cancellation therefore comes from the supported fair row at \(X_1\), not from choosing a tautological query.

It remains to count the mandatory incidence records.  An event-consistent complete target assignment first chooses the common value of \(x_1=x_{k+1}\) in two ways and then chooses \(x_2,\ldots,x_k\) freely in \(2^{k-1}\) ways.  Therefore
\[
 \# B_k=2\cdot 2^{k-1}=2^k.
\]
The definition of \(Ictx\) requires a separate record for every event-consistent complete target-assignment term.  The checker in \texttt{def:checker} verifies exhaustive lexicographic indexing of those records and rejects an omission.  Thus every \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) contains all \(2^k\) records.  In the fixed tagged, length-delimited grammar of \texttt{def:certificate-grammar}, each explicit record contributes at least one symbol, so the encoded output length is \(\Omega(2^k)\).  In the standard bit-cost model, writing an output of that length also takes \(\Omega(2^k)\) time.

Finally, suppose a compiler for the present grammar had time and output length bounded by a polynomial in the explicit grounding size times a factor exponential only in \(w\).  On the constructed family, the grounding size is \(O(k)\) and \(w=0\), so that bound would be polynomial in \(k\).  This contradicts the lower bound \(\Omega(2^k)\).  Exact variable elimination can compute the constant polynomial \(1/2\) compactly, but the current checker still demands the exhaustive assignment-level \(Ictx\).  Hence the obstruction is specific to the frozen grammar and does not decide whether a replacement circuit-level incidence grammar admits a width-sensitive compiler.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under the present certificate grammar and checker, the answer to the proof-carrying compiler question is negative.  For every integer \(k\geq 1\), there is an explicit finite acyclic target grounding and compact equality-query description whose combined pre-incidence input size is \(O(k)\), whose target ground graph is edgeless and hence has treewidth \(w=0\), and which has binary variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_{k+1}\), no intervention, target event \(B=\{X_1=X_{k+1}\}\), a fair supported row at \(X_1\), and the unsupported binary row \(rstar\) at \(X_{k+1}\).  The row \(rstar\) is directly event-relevant and the replayed target polynomial is the nontrivial constant \(F=1/2\), while the mandated \(Ictx\) contains exactly \(2^k\) event-consistent complete target-assignment records.  Consequently, every compiler that outputs an \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) has time and output length \(\Omega(2^k)\).  Thus no bound polynomial in the explicit grounding size and exponential only in \(w\) is possible for this exhaustive assignment-level grammar.  This conclusion does not rule out a width-sensitive compiler after replacement of \(Ictx\) and \(Check\) by a compact circuit-level incidence grammar and checker.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The sure-event witness is too weak for the mandated maximality claim because it does not make the unsupported row directly relevant to the query. The replacement restricts the witness to the required compact equality-event family and proves the same grammar obstruction with a non-tautological probability.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Given \(S\), \(G\), \(\rho\), \(a\), \(B\), and \(K\), exact variable elimination along a supplied bounded-width tree decomposition of the acyclic target grounding may represent messages by fraction-free univariate arithmetic circuits that preserve every type--context key and may produce the dense \(F\) together with compact local gate identities.  Under the present assignment-level interface, however, an output accepted by \(Check\) must also materialize the complete \(Ictx\) for \((\rho,a,B)\), including one record for every event-consistent complete target assignment; this last step may require exhaustive expansion.  Accordingly, this handle asserts no width-sensitive time or output bound for the present \(Ictx\) and \(Check\).  Such a guarantee requires a replacement circuit-level incidence grammar and checker.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The existing construction incorrectly promises production of the exhaustive assignment-level incidence table without exhaustive expansion. The corrected construction separates compact variable elimination from the mandatory explicit-incidence output step and leaves circuit-level certification open.
